result.question: What did captain say in letter to Felix?

readings.answer: He wrote that the Jews had seized the man and were about to kill him, but he rescued him with his troops, and that the case concerned their law with no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.
readings.support: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him | I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment

assessments.reason: The reading explicitly says the case concerned their (Jewish) law, which matches v.29, and added details (rescue, no capital charge) are also in vv.27–29.

result.reason: The answer includes that the accusations concerned Jewish law (v.29), matching the key, with only supported extra detail.
